answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent network employs radio-frequency physical-layer fingerprinting. Nodes authenticate peers by measuring transient amplifier non-linearities emitted from each transmitter's sable casing. Because analog hardware imperfections cannot be virtualized, an attacker must purchase discrete RF transceivers per identity. However, multipath reflections across a river or canyon distort waveforms, occasionally triggering false rejections of valid agents.
